{"id": "2:204/q11", "question": "What does yuʿjibuka convey?", "turns_on": "Whether the root's literal wonder or its contextual pleasure is foregrounded.", "positions": [{"id": "2:204/q11/p1", "position": "His speech pleases, impresses, inclines or looms large to the listener.", "reasons": "ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r5 (رجل من ثقيف; reports): A report says a man from Thaqīf impressed the Prophet with his speech while inwardly concealing the opposite of his attractive outward presentation. NAHHAS:v1p297/r9 (الحسن; reports): Al-Ḥasan identifies the person whose speech impresses as a liar; other reported identifications are a wrongdoer or a hypocrite. THALABI:v2p122/r1 (author; holds): Here يعجبك conveys approval and love for good-sounding speech; for disapproval one says عجبت من كذا. WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p74/r2 (author; holds): The qualification in worldly life reflects his lying: the Prophet was not truly impressed with his words, and al-Akhnas earns no afterlife reward for them. WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r6 (author; holds): His speech impresses people only in worldly life and earns no reward in the Hereafter. JISHUMI:v1p835/r4 (author; holds): The speech pleases Muhammad and looms large in his heart; the speaker claims belief and loyalty, and invokes God as witness while inwardly concealing the opposite. BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r2 (author; holds): The speech pleases the listener and grows weighty in the heart; Arabic uses «I like this» for approval but «I am amazed at this» for dislike or disapproval. KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r1 (author; holds): His speech pleases you and looms large in your heart; something amazing is what seems great to the mind. KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r5 (author; reports): Alternatively, it modifies “pleases you”: his eloquence impresses in this life, but not at judgment when he stammers or is not permitted to speak. TABRISI:2:204-205/r17 (author; holds): The hypocrite's speech pleases Muhammad and makes a strong impression. RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r1 (author; holds): يعجبك means his speech pleases you and grows large in your estimation, like something wondrous that looms in the mind. RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r2 (author; holds): One reading takes the phrase as speech that impresses when he seeks worldly interests, like admiring someone’s words on a particular matter. BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r1 (author; holds): His speech pleases you and grows impressive in your estimation; wonder is perplexity caused by ignorance of what prompted the surprise. BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r3 (author; holds): Alternatively, his eloquence delights listeners in this life but not the next, when astonishment and speechlessness overtake him or he is not permitted to speak. NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r2 (author; holds): His speech pleases and impresses; the root sense is something marvelous that looms large in the mind. NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r3 (author; reports): The phrase may modify ‘his speech’: he seeks worldly advantage through professed love, not the afterlife; or it may modify ‘pleases you’: his eloquence charms in this life but fails him in the next. ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r2 (الزمخشري; rejects): Al-Zamakhshari allows attachment to يعجبك, so the speech impresses in worldly life but not at resurrection when he is held back or barred from speaking; Abu Hayyan calls this remote. ITQAN:v4p384/r9 (author; holds): The person whose speech impresses the listener is al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq. BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r3 (author; reports): One reading links the phrase to the speech: the person pleases you by what he says about worldly life, seeking worldly advantage rather than the Hereafter.
